reason: Project lens, checked against the source. Not protected, not generated, no data or table moves, no new RAM, not raster-timed. Writes the same zero page as the old code (sky_j8 &E1, sky_stop &E2, s_ptr &C2/&C3). Their final values change (sky_stop = sk, not Ystart - rn; s_ptr = rl + offset, not rl), but nothing reads them first: lead_col's callers in sky.6502 do BCS fall and reload A from sky_c, and every later user (sky_row in sky_main, sky_col_row in sky_edges, sky_draw, sky_zero, sky_check) writes s_ptr/sky_stop before reading. The interrupt does not use them. It reads exactly the same 16-bit screen addresses as before. rl + (rt|sk) - rn + 1 is never negative because the builder (sky_geom) gives rn = L+1 with rt = L for the bottom row, rn = 8 with rt = 7 for whole rows, rn = 1..8 with rt = 7 for the top row, and the split copies keep both. Since rt|sk >= rt >= rn-1, the reads land in the same RAM under whatever ROMSEL/ACCCON X state the caller has, and reads have no side effects. sky_col_row is kept for sky_edges' sky_col_zero. Room: about 70 bytes against 27 (+43), so hazel_b_end goes from &DF65 to about &DF90, under the &E000 ASSERT. The startup copy count is 16-bit (LO/HI of hazel_b_end - hazel_a_end). The MGAME file grows 43 bytes against about 1,500 free under &5A80, and kindcache's use of hazel_b_end applies only in SKY_HELI=0 builds, where sky_hazel is not included. Behaviour is the same: C is set exactly when some byte is non-zero. The dirty path is slower (it finishes the row and does not exit early), but it measured 0 times, and its worst case is still below the old clean scan. Minor: the new comment '(its caller here only)' wrongly suggests sky_col_row has no other caller (sky_edges calls it), which is harmless. Recount: a full rn=8 row is 187 -> 142 cycles, rn=1 is 82 -> 74, and an out-of-entry row 29 -> about 12. The claimed ~40 a call is plausible.
